key_insight: MANTRA reconstructs multiscale turbulent velocity fields from sparse, irregular measurements using continuous tensor-product representations constrained to low-rank Tucker manifolds.
engineering_relevance: The framework can extract coherent flow structures from limited experimental measurements without requiring gridded observations or governing equations.
method: Represent each velocity component in a continuous tensor-product space.
Fit low-rank Tucker coefficient tensors using Riemannian optimization.
Adapt tensor rank and basis complexity to capture coordinate-wise spatiotemporal correlations.
evidence_signal: Tests on forced isotropic turbulence and cylinder flow report reconstruction at sampling densities orders of magnitude below the simulation grids and accuracy under Gaussian noise up to 20% of peak velocity, alongside an experimental oscillating-jet demonstration.
watch_item: Performance beyond the tested flows remains uncertain, particularly when sparse measurements do not sufficiently constrain the chosen low-rank representation.
paper_title: Low-Rank Tensor Manifolds for Turbulent Field Reconstruction from Sparse Data
